note: A 21-year-old second-year medical student with roughly $900 to his name, living with parents who pay 1,500 euros a month for his schooling. He is not yet successful in the terms the ICP states - it names physicians, and he is four years from being one - and he is a long way from 'makes good money', which he disclosed himself before any price was quoted. Health is also not his neglected area; he trains four times a week and it is the part of his life he protects, which is why the good-to-great and not-deconditioned criteria are the two he meets cleanly. Judged against the criteria as written he is outside, and the commercial outcome matched. Two findings sit underneath the score. First, the stated ICP would have screened him out on income, and on income alone that was correct - but it would have screened him out for the wrong reason, because the criterion that should have stopped this call is one the ICP does not contain: he arrived with active shin and femur fractures and a post-surgical shoulder. Second, he is the clearest case in the batch of intent and fit being decoupled from ability to pay at a point in time - 'as soon as I can afford it, I know I will do it' - which the income screen treats as a permanent disqualification rather than a timing problem.
